name: Light Congo Pink
lede: Light Congo Pink is a soft apricot pink from Ridgway's 1912 atlas, a lighter sibling of the deeper Congo Pink rather than a color with its own separate history.

sections.title: A lighter Congo Pink
sections.body:
Ridgway's 1912 atlas carries this tone on plate XXVIII, hue 7″, notated 0.1YR 7.5/4.4 in the Munsell system [1]. The 1955 ISCC-NBS dictionary groups it under block 28, naming it light yellowish pink, 2.6 units from Ridgway's reading [1].

Its closest neighbor in our library is [[rose-dawn]], about 2.7 units away, close enough to pass for the same color [2]. [[indian-pink]] sits about 3.8 units off and darker, and [[flesh-pink]] and [[flesh-color]] about 5.2 to 5.5 units off and lighter [2]. "Congo" names the base color this one lightens; what made the base color Congo in the first place is not explained in Ridgway's text [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body:
Our archive matches this tone in 148 of 23,781 paintings, about 0.62 percent, as photographed, more common than 54 percent of the named colors tracked [3]. It peaks in the 1900s, present in 1.1 percent of the 1,674 paintings from that decade, 3.3 times its museums' expected rate [3].

Inside a painting it most often plays a light tone, in 40 percent of its 72 clearly-ranked appearances, a rank computed within each canvas so varnish cannot fake it [3]. In printed English the phrase's use peaked in the 1940s, though that Ngram count covers every sense of the words, not only the color [3]. These are photographs of aged, varnished paintings, and the match is a computed color reading, not a pigment identification [3].

origin.named_after: a lighter variant of Congo Pink; the origin of "Congo" itself is undocumented here
origin.source: Ridgway, Color Standards and Color Nomenclature; ISCC-NBS, NBS Circular 553

questions.q: Light Congo Pink is Ridgway's lighter version of which color?
True or false: Ridgway's text explains why the base color is called Congo.

openers: Light Congo Pink is close enough to Rose Dawn that the two are nearly interchangeable on screen.
